criteria.statement: Repository, remote, default branch, and project identity are ChangeBridge only.
The exact Stage 3 commit, tree, and continuation checkpoint are verified.
All predecessor validators pass and protected evidence remains byte-identical.
Stage 4 scope, non-goals, write surface, dependencies, and claims are frozen.
A clean disposable environment installs only repository-declared dependencies.
The checksum-pinned qualified Iceberg runtime is used without dependency drift.
The apply manifest binds generation, predecessor, source history, S, terminal frontier, and transactions.
Manifest identity and transaction digests use the accepted canonicalization profile.
PostgreSQL LSNs are parsed and compared as typed 64-bit positions.
Only events in the open-closed interval (S,F] are admitted.
Transaction and event order are deterministic and duplicate sequence identities fail closed.
Transaction completeness is proven against declared event count, IDs, digest, tables, and commit LSN.
Foreign generations and undeclared transactions fail before target mutation.
Insert, update, and delete image shapes are validated before apply.
Unapproved schema or primary-key evolution is deferred to Stage 5 and fails closed.
The Stage 3 snapshot candidate is the only eligible starting state.
The complete accepted post-S transaction is preserved through the unchanged Stage 2 normalizer.
The durable control store records checkpoints, transaction claims, table receipts, and tombstones.
Transaction identity replay with changed content fails closed.
Per-table input digests and commit tokens are deterministic.
Target before-image preconditions detect drift before mutation.
Real Spark executes the accepted update as an Iceberg MERGE in the candidate generation.
Iceberg snapshot summaries bind generation, transaction, manifest, frontier, and input digests.
Commit identity is discoverable from Iceberg after control-process loss.
A recovered commit is verified and receipted without a blind rewrite.
Checkpoint advancement requires durable receipts for every manifest-declared table.
Checkpoint advancement uses compare-and-swap revision and predecessor frontier guards.
A fully checkpointed identical replay is a no-op.
Deletes retain auditable tombstone provenance even though the accepted fixture contains no delete.
The independent SQLite reference adapter applies the same transaction semantics.
Real Iceberg and independent reference row counts match after F.
Real Iceberg and independent reference canonical table digests match after F.
The accepted order update produces amount 4750 and campaign post-boundary.
The final accepted target remains six orders and 66 order items.
Two clean real-target runs produce identical logical projections.
A process exit after Iceberg commit leaves the checkpoint at S.
Recovery advances exactly once to 0/194FE20 without another Iceberg write.
Injected target drift fails with a stable before-image mismatch diagnostic.
The generation remains CDC_APPLYING and unpublished after Stage 4.
No atomic cross-Iceberg-table or production exactly-once claim is made.
Unit, property, integration, differential, and failure tests cover the protocol.
CI acquires the existing checksum-pinned runtime and runs Stage 4 validation.
Evidence is source-commit/tree bound, schema-valid, complete, and free of transient paths and secrets.
The exact reviewed PR head passes every Stage 4 candidate gate.
The guarded merge succeeds only for the reviewed head under repository policy.
Fresh merged main resolves to the expected merge and preserves the reviewed Stage 4 tree.
Fresh merged main passes all frozen and Stage 4 validators.
The external PART2_STAGE4_CDC_APPLY_VERIFIED checkpoint records exact identities, evidence, limitations, and Stage 5 entry.
